questions.text: What is the central idea of the passage?
options: Private vehicles should be banned in every city.
Effective public transport requires reliable services and thoughtful planning.
Increasing the number of buses always solves transport problems.
Rail services are unnecessary in urban areas.

passage.text: Public transport systems can contribute to more efficient and accessible cities. Reliable buses and rail services may reduce dependence on private vehicles, particularly when routes connect residential areas with workplaces, schools and essential services. However, simply expanding the number of buses is not sufficient. Passengers also need safe stops, accurate service information, reasonable waiting times and convenient connections between routes. Transport planning is therefore most effective when infrastructure, service quality and the needs of different groups of passengers are considered together.

questions.explanation: The passage explains what effective public transport needs.
